name: GPT-1
notes: First GPT model, decoder-only transformer. Trained for 30 days on 8 P600 GPUs .

name: BERT
notes: An early and influential language model. Encoder-only and thus not built to be prompted or generative. Training took 4 days on 64 TPUv2 chips.

name: T5
notes: Base model for Google projects like Imagen.

name: XLNet
notes: An alternative to BERT; designed as encoder-only. Trained on 512 TPU v3 chips for 5.5 days.

name: GPT-2
notes: Trained on 32 TPUv3 chips for 1 week.

name: GPT-3
notes: A fine-tuned variant of GPT-3, termed GPT-3.5, was made available to the public through ChatGPT in 2022.

name: GPT-Neo
notes: The first of a series of free GPT-3 alternatives released by EleutherAI. GPT-Neo outperformed an equivalent-size GPT-3 model on some benchmarks, but was significantly worse than the largest GPT-3.

name: HyperCLOVA
notes: Its technical report says the model is the "first discovery on near 100B-scale non-English LM" by "constructing a large Korean-centric corpus of 560B tokens."

name: Megatron-Turing NLG
notes: Trained for 3 months on over 2000 A100 GPUs on the NVIDIA Selene Supercomputer , for over 3 million GPU-hours.

name: Claude
notes: Fine-tuned for desirable behavior in conversations.

name: PaLM (Pathways Language Model)
notes: Trained for ~60 days on ~6000 TPU v4 chips.

name: OPT (Open Pretrained Transformer)
notes: GPT-3 architecture with some adaptations from Megatron. The training logbook written by the team was published.

name: Minerva
corpus: 38.5B tokens from webpages filtered for math content and from arXiv
notes: For solving "mathematical and scientific questions using step-by-step reasoning".

name: BLOOM
developer: Large collaboration led by Hugging Face

name: Falcon
corpus: 1T tokens, from RefinedWeb (filtered web text corpus) plus some "curated corpora".

name: BloombergGPT
corpus: 363B tokens from Bloomberg's proprietary data sources, plus 345B tokens from general purpose datasets
notes: Designed for financial tasks.

name: PaLM 2 (Pathways Language Model 2)
notes: Used in the Bard chatbot.

name: Phi-1
notes: Trained for 4 days on 8 A100s.

name: Llama 2
notes: Trained over 3.3 million GPU (A100) hours.

name: Claude 2
notes: Used in the Claude chatbot.

name: Granite 13b
notes: Used in IBM Watsonx .

name: Claude 2.1
notes: Used in the Claude chatbot. Has a context window of 200,000 tokens, or ~500 pages.

name: Grok-1
notes: Used in the Grok chatbot. Grok 1 has a context length of 8,192 tokens and has access to X (Twitter).

name: Gemini 1.0
notes: Multimodal model, comes in three sizes. Used in the chatbot of the same name .

name: Mixtral 8x7B
notes: Outperforms GPT-3.5 and Llama 2 70B on many benchmarks. Mixture of experts model, with 12.9 billion parameters activated per token.

name: DeepSeek-LLM
notes: Trained on English and Chinese text. Used 10 training FLOPs for 67B model, 10 FLOPs for 7B.

name: Phi-2
notes: Trained on real and synthetic "textbook-quality" data over 14 days on 96 A100 GPUs.

name: Gemini 1.5
notes: Multimodal model based on a MoE architecture. Context window above 1 million tokens.

name: Claude 3
notes: Includes three models: Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus.

name: Fugaku-LLM
developer: Fujitsu , Tokyo Institute of Technology , Tohoku University , RIKEN , etc.
notes: The largest model ever trained on CPU-only, on the Fugaku supercomputer; the model was trained from scratch on 380 billion tokens using 13,824 Fugaku nodes.

name: Phi-3
notes: Marketed by Microsoft as a "small language model".

name: DeepSeek-V2
notes: 1.4M hours on H800.

name: Nemotron -4
notes: Trained for 1 epoch. Trained on 6144 H100 GPUs between December 2023 and May 2024.

name: Claude 3.5
notes: Initially, only one model, Sonnet, was released. In October 2024, Sonnet 3.5 was upgraded, and Haiku 3.5 became available.

name: Llama 3.1
notes: 405B version took 31 million hours on H100 -80GB, at 3.8E25 FLOPs.

name: Grok-2
notes: Originally closed-source, then re-released as "Grok 2.5" under a source-available license in August 2025.

name: OpenAI o1
notes: First LLM described as a " reasoning model ".

name: Sarvam-1
notes: Supports 10 Indic languages and English

name: Mistral Large
notes: Upgraded over time. The latest version is 24.11.

name: Pixtral
notes: Multimodal. There is also a 12B version which is under Apache 2 license.

name: Phi-4
notes: Marketed by Microsoft as a "small language model".

name: DeepSeek-V3
notes: Used 2.788M training hours on H800 GPUs. Originally released under the DeepSeek License, then re-released under the MIT License as "DeepSeek-V3-0324" in March 2025.

name: Amazon Nova
notes: Includes three models: Nova Micro, Nova Lite, and Nova Pro.

name: DeepSeek-R1
notes: No pretraining; reinforcement-learned upon V3-Base.

name: Qwen2.5
notes: 7 dense models with parameter counts from 0.5B to 72B. Alibaba also released 2 MoE variants.

name: Gemini 2.0
notes: Three models released: Flash, Flash-Lite and Pro.

name: Grok 3
notes: Training cost claimed to be "10x the compute of previous state-of-the-art models".

name: Claude 3.7
notes: One model, Sonnet 3.7.

name: GPT-4.5
notes: OpenAI's largest non-reasoning model at the time.

name: Gemini 2.5
notes: Three models released: Flash, Flash-Lite and Pro.

name: OpenAI o3 and o4-mini
notes: Reasoning models.

name: Qwen3
notes: Multiple sizes, the smallest being 0.6B.

name: Claude 4
notes: Includes two models, Sonnet and Opus.

name: Sarvam-M
notes: Hybrid reasoning model fine-tuned on Mistral Small base; optimized for math, programming, and Indian languages.

name: Param-1
notes: Corpus is "focus[ed] on India’s linguistic landscape".

name: GLM-4.5
notes: Released in 355B and 106B sizes. Corpus size was calculated by combining the 15 trillion tokens and the 7 trillion tokens pre-training mix.

name: GPT-OSS
notes: Released in 20B and 120B sizes.

name: Claude 4.1
notes: Includes one model, Opus.

name: GPT-5
notes: Includes three models: GPT-5, GPT-5 mini, and GPT-5 nano. GPT-5 is available in ChatGPT and API. It includes reasoning abilities.

name: DeepSeek-V3.1
notes: Corpus size based on DeepSeek V3 (trained on 14.8T tokens); further trained on 839B tokens from the extension phases (630B + 209B). A hybrid model that can switch between thinking and non-thinking modes.

name: Apertus
notes: The first LLM to be compliant with the Artificial Intelligence Act of the European Union .

name: Gemini 3
notes: Models released: Deep Think and Pro.

name: Olmo 3
notes: Includes 7B and 32B parameter versions, alongside reasoning and instruction-following models.

name: Claude Opus 4.5
notes: Largest model in the Claude family.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2
notes: Uses a custom DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) mechanism

name: GPT 5.2
notes: It was able to solve an open problem in statistical learning theory that had previously remained unresolved by human researchers.

name: Qwen3-Max-Thinking
notes: Proprietary reasoning model with adaptive tool-use, test-time scaling, and iterative self-reflection.

name: Kimi K2.5
notes: Multimodal MoE with 32B active parameters, derived from Kimi K2. Can use "Agent Swarm" technology to coordinate up to 100 parallel sub-agents.

name: Step 3.5 Flash
notes: MoE model with 11B active parameters out of 196B total

name: GLM-5
notes: 40B active parameters

name: Qwen3.5
notes: 17B active parameters

name: Param-2
notes: Mixture-of-experts model, successor of Param-1; many more Indic languages are supported. Trained on H100 GPUs for 24 days.

name: Sarvam-105B
notes: India's first independently-trained foundation model; has 105B and 30B versions. Based on mixture-of-experts model, using only 10.3B active parameters at a time. Interprets Indic languages and Hinglish .

name: Sarvam-30B
notes: India's first independently-trained foundation model; has 105B and 30B versions. Based on mixture-of-experts model, using only 10.3B active parameters at a time. Interprets Indic languages and Hinglish .

name: Mistral Small 4
notes: MoE model with 6B active parameters out of 119B total

name: MiMo-V2-Pro
notes: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) model with more than 1 trillion parameters (43 billion active). Designed for agentic scenarios. Initially available on OpenRouter under the codename "Hunter Alpha" before official release.

name: Gemma 4
notes: Released in 31B, 26B A4B (3.8B active parameters), E4B (4B effective parameters), and E2B variants

name: GLM-5.1
notes: 40B active parameters

name: Qwen3.6
notes: MoE model with 3B active parameters out of 35B total

name: Kimi K2.6
notes: 32B active parameters

name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
notes: Preview release

name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
notes: Preview release

name: MiMo-V2.5-Pro
notes: MoE model designed for agentic coding and long-horizon software engineering tasks.

name: MiMo-V2.5
notes: Omni-modal MoE model with agentic capabilities and 1M-token context.

name: Mistral Medium 3.5
notes: Mistral AI's flagship model that merges instruction-following, reasoning, and coding into a single 128B dense model

name: Step 3.7 Flash
notes: Parameter count is 196B (base) + 1.8B ( ViT ).

name: MiniMax-M3
notes: 23B active parameters

name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
notes: 55B active parameters

name: Kimi K2.7 Code
notes: 32B active parameters

name: GLM-5.2
notes: 40B active parameters

name: LongCat-2.0
notes: 48B active parameters. Preview version previously released as "Owl Alpha" on OpenRouter.

name: Hy3
notes: 21B active parameters

name: Inkling
notes: 41B active parameters

name: Kimi K3
notes: Moonshot AI announced that weights will be released by 27 July

name: Qwen3.8-Max
notes: Preview release. Alibaba announced that weights will be released at a later date.
